items.title: CVS will split up its pharmacy and insurance business into two companies, WSJ says
items.summary: Nov 3 (Reuters) - CVS Health plans to break up its $117 billion business, separating its retail pharmacies from the Caremark pharmacy benefit management operations and the Aetna insurance company it bought nearly a decade ago, the Wall Street Journal quoted the company as saying on Tuesday. CVS Health, which is set to report quarterly results on ‌Wednesday, did not respond to a Reuters request for comment.

items.title: CVS Health to split into two publicly traded companies by 2028, FT reports
items.summary: Investing.com-- CVS Health Corp (NYSE:CVS) is planning to split its retail pharmacy business from its insurance operations, potentially unwinding one of the U.S. healthcare industry’s largest vertical integration deals, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.

items.title: CVS Stock Rises After Hours On Alleged Pharmacy Spin-Off Ahead Of Q3 Earnings Report
items.summary: CVS is considering spinning off its retail pharmacy division as a separately listed company, The Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

items.title: CVS Will Break Off Its Namesake Pharmacies

items.title: CVS Jumps on Report It Plans to Break Up Health Conglomerate
items.summary: CVS Health Corp. is discussing plans to spin off its retail pharmacy business, according to the Financial Times, a shocking retreat for the country’s largest drugstore chain.
